# Horizun PBI MCP

> Open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for local Power BI Desktop
> and `.pbip` projects. It connects Claude, Codex and other MCP clients to a
> live Power BI Desktop session and to Power BI project files on disk.

## Canonical links

- Repository: https://github.com/HorizunGroup/horizun-pbi-mcp
- Latest stable release: https://github.com/HorizunGroup/horizun-pbi-mcp/releases/latest
- Installation and client setup: https://github.com/HorizunGroup/horizun-pbi-mcp/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md
- Full tool catalogue (117 tools): https://github.com/HorizunGroup/horizun-pbi-mcp/blob/main/docs/TOOL_CATALOG.md
- Architecture and invariants: https://github.com/HorizunGroup/horizun-pbi-mcp/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- Security model: https://github.com/HorizunGroup/horizun-pbi-mcp/blob/main/docs/SECURITY.md
- Tutorial, install to first dashboard: https://github.com/HorizunGroup/horizun-pbi-mcp/blob/main/docs/TUTORIAL.md
- Horizun Hub ecosystem: https://horizunhub.com

## What it does

Horizun PBI MCP covers two complementary layers of Power BI automation.
The live layer (Power BI Desktop open on `localhost:<port>`) queries data
with DAX, documents the semantic model, and creates or edits measures via
ADOMD.NET and TOM through `pythonnet`. The on-disk layer edits `.pbip`
projects directly through TMDL (semantic model) and PBIR (report), so it can
generate and arrange visuals and pages durably, edit-file by edit-file.

The local live endpoint only ever exposes the data layer of the semantic
model; visuals, pages and layout are never touched through it or through any
live API — those are edited exclusively through PBIR files. The server
enforces that separation instead of trying to move visuals live.

v1.0.1 ships 117 tools, backed by 1547 passing tests (3 skipped, each with
its documented condition). Two validation layers check every PBIR edit
before it is written, and non-read-only DAX is blocked by a fail-closed
classifier.

## How to use it

Register the server with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, or any stdio
MCP client, then point it at a running Power BI Desktop instance or a
`.pbip` project on disk. See docs/INSTALL.md for exact client configuration
and docs/TOOL_INVENTORY.md for the 34-tool baseline surface with risk class
and preconditions per tool.
